verdicts.claim: Architecture: NemotronHForCausalLM, 42 layers, pattern gives 21 Mamba2 / 4 attention / 17 MLP, 8 KV heads, head_dim 128, no sliding window, max_position_embeddings 262144
KV bytes per token 16384 (BF16) / 8192 (FP8); vLLM pool 14.65 - 7.40 - 1.2 = 6.05 GiB gives about 396k tokens BF16 KV, capped at 262144 (4.0 GiB)
verdicts.correction: Recomputed: 2 x 4 x 8 x 128 x 2 = 16384 B. 262144 x 16384 = 4.00 GiB. Mamba state per sequence with fp32 SSM cache: 21 x (96x80x128x4 + (7680+2x8x128) x 3 x 2) = 83.8 MB (79.9 MiB), matches. vLLM's hybrid allocator inflates the attention block size to match the Mamba page size, and Mamba groups take blocks from the same pool, so the real token count is somewhat lower than 396k. With 6.05 GiB minus 4 sequences of Mamba state there is still about 1.7 GiB of headroom above 262144 (inferred from method, not a vLLM run).

verdicts.claim: No open vLLM issue specific to this model or to sm_120
verdicts.correction: Nothing for Nemotron-3-Nano-4B or dense NemotronH on sm_120 turned up. Adjacent open issues: #52225 (Xid 13 warp errors on SM120 under multi-hour load with hybrid Mamba Nemotron-3.5-Lightning NVFP4 Marlin MoE, seen on RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell). It involves a different model and quant, but the hybrid Mamba path on SM120 is shared, so it is a stability risk to watch. Also #51250 (prefix caching ineffective on Mamba/GDN hybrids, a performance matter for agentic multi-turn use) and #55894 (Mamba+MTP corruption, does not apply without MTP).

verdicts.claim: llama.cpp --jinja tool calling should work for this model
verdicts.correction: Open llama.cpp PR #30193 (2026-10-08, still open) says tool-call argument grammars enforce declared JSON key order, and that this breaks tool calls for Nemotron and Qwen models. Its author's replay measured 0 to 3 valid tool calls out of 32 on master and 25 to 29 with the patch. So llama.cpp tool calling for this model family is contested on master. Prefer vLLM, or test with OpenCode's real tool schemas before relying on it.

verdicts.correction: Best realistic configuration: vLLM v0.33.0 with the BF16 checkpoint, --max-model-len 262144 (or 131072), qwen3_coder plus nemotron_v3, and capabilities.tools enabled manually in OpenCode. FP8 is a speed option only. llama.cpp is the fallback, but tool calling there is caveated by PR #30193.

summary:
I could not refute any runtime claim. Every load-bearing value matched on a raw re-read: the config (21 Mamba, 4 attention and 17 MLP layers; 8 KV heads; head_dim 128; 262144 max positions), the HF file sizes, KV at 16384 B/token, Mamba state at about 80 MiB per sequence, and a vLLM KV pool of 6.05 GiB that holds the full 262144 context (4.0 GiB of BF16 KV). In vLLM v0.33.0 the registry, qwen3_coder, nemotron_v3 and --default-chat-template-kwargs are all present at the cited lines. In llama.cpp b12418, nemotron-h.cpp is present and the chat template is byte-identical (md5 match).

Corrections and caveats:
(1) Open llama.cpp PR #30193 reports that tool-call grammars enforce JSON key order, and that this breaks Nemotron and Qwen tool calls on master (0 to 3 of 32 valid in the author's replay). llama.cpp tool calling is therefore contested, not merely untested.
(2) Open vLLM issue #52225 reports Xid warp errors on SM120 with a hybrid Mamba Nemotron 3.5 NVFP4 model under long load. It is a different model, but the Mamba path on SM120 is shared, so treat it as a stability risk. Open issue #51250 reports that prefix caching is ineffective on Mamba hybrids.
(3) The FP8 repo createdAt is 2026-03-12, and the exact FP8 total is 5,267,055,808 B.
(4) vLLM's hybrid page-size unification reduces the theoretical 396k token figure, but there is still ample headroom at 262144.

Verdict stands: it serves OpenCode with tool calls and at least 64k context on vLLM, and agentic quality is weak.

Gaps: I made no live run. sm_120 Mamba stability is unverified, and so is the exact vLLM block allocation. I did not check whether PR #30193 affects flat-argument tools of the kind OpenCode mostly uses.
